title: In which Indian city is Athulya Senior Care headquartered?
explanation: Athulya Senior Care is a Chennai-based eldercare operator.

title: Which global private equity firm is backing Athulya Senior Care?
explanation: Athulya Senior Care is backed by Morgan Stanley Private Equity.

title: What is the name of Athulya’s overseas senior care facility in Mauritius?
explanation: Athulya is setting up its "Chez Moi" facility in Mauritius.

title: Besides Mauritius, which two overseas markets is Athulya planning expansion into?
explanation: Athulya plans international expansion into Sri Lanka and Dubai.

title: Which demographic is Athulya targeting for culturally aligned care in Mauritius and Sri Lanka?
explanation: Athulya targets the Tamil diaspora in Mauritius and Sri Lanka for familiar cultural care.

title: Which countries/institutions has Athulya signed MoUs with to export skilled care manpower?
explanation: Athulya signed MoUs with Singapore’s SingHealth and Japan for exporting care professionals.

title: How many total senior care beds does Athulya currently manage?
explanation: Athulya currently manages 1,500 beds, with 900 operational.

title: What is Athulya’s approximate monthly revenue from its operational beds?
explanation: Athulya generates approximately Rs. 8.5 crore monthly from its operations.

title: By 2030, how much is India’s organized senior care market projected to expand?
explanation: India’s organized senior care capacity is projected to grow from 20,000 to 100,000 units.

title: What top-line revenue target has Athulya set to support its planned FY32 IPO?
explanation: Athulya is targeting a Rs. 1,000 crore top-line to support its planned FY32 IPO.

title: What EBITDA target has Athulya outlined for its FY32 IPO roadmap?
explanation: Athulya is targeting Rs. 250 crore EBITDA to support its planned FY32 IPO.

title: How large is the global eldercare industry projected to grow over the coming decade?
options: From US$ 1 billion to US$ 2 billion
From US$ 100 billion to US$ 120 billion
From US$ 15 billion to US$ 50 billion
From US$ 500 million to US$ 1 billion
explanation: The eldercare sector is projected to expand from US$ 15 billion to US$ 50 billion.

title: According to the World Health Organization (WHO), what demographic percentage will the over-60 population cross?
explanation: The WHO expects the global over-60 demographic to cross 22% of total population.

title: What asset structure does Athulya utilize to expand into international markets?
options: Asset-light operational partnerships and specialized workforce export
Building massive retirement islands from scratch
Operating purely via virtual telemedicine calls
explanation: Athulya pairs asset-light operational tie-ups abroad with specialized workforce export.

title: Which pioneer in senior living and mental healthcare was cited for early-career campus recruitment?
explanation: Cadabams recently offered an early-career opportunity for campus talent in senior care.

title: What career capabilities are required to scale eldercare services across international borders?
options: Stock day trading and crypto mining
Client acquisition, cross-border ops, regulatory compliance, and business development
explanation: Cross-border eldercare needs client acquisition, regulatory compliance, and ops leadership.

title: Why is eldercare evolving into a cross-border healthcare and real estate asset class?
options: Retirement homes are exempt from all taxes worldwide
Aging global populations and rising demand for specialized geriatric care
Seniors are legally required to move overseas
explanation: Global aging demographics are transforming senior living into an institutional asset class.

title: What customer segment is Athulya targeting in Dubai?
options: High-net-worth Indian expatriates navigating the local ecosystem
explanation: In Dubai, Athulya targets high-net-worth Indian expatriates seeking trusted care.

title: How does exporting trained geriatric care manpower benefit Indian eldercare operators?
options: Eliminates all operational costs in Chennai
Forces operators to exit the domestic market
Solves global talent shortages while unlocking higher profit margins
explanation: Exporting specialized care workers addresses global shortages while yielding higher margins.

title: What key friction do elderly expatriates face in overseas locations like Mauritius?
options: Healthcare is completely illegal for seniors
Local facilities lack culturally aligned care and language familiarity
Seniors are barred from living in Mauritius
explanation: Expatriates often struggle to find culturally aligned geriatric care and language support.

title: In which fiscal year does Athulya Senior Care plan to launch its public IPO?
explanation: Athulya has laid out a roadmap targeting a public listing in FY32.

title: What type of service delivery model does institutional eldercare represent?
options: A high-touch, human-centric assisted living model
explanation: Eldercare is inherently a high-touch, compassionate, service-intensive delivery model.

title: Why was the lack of student nominations for Cadabams described as a missed opportunity?
options: Cadabams only hires once every 50 years
Healthcare salaries are capped by law
Senior living has zero future job opportunities
Eldercare is a booming US$ 50B sunrise sector with massive career growth upside
explanation: Eldercare is a high-growth US$ 50B sunrise industry offering immense leadership upside.

title: What core advantage does Athulya’s institutional private equity backing provide?
options: Long-term capital stability, governance standards, and rapid bed expansion
explanation: Morgan Stanley’s backing provides institutional governance, capital strength, and scale.

title: What overarching strategic takeaway emerges from Athulya’s global expansion?
options: Senior living should remain strictly local and unorganized
Indian healthcare operators can build scalable, cross-border institutional platforms
Overseas elderly populations have zero care needs
Workforce export has no commercial viability
explanation: Athulya proves that Indian care operators can build scalable, high-margin global platforms.
